preconditions.description: The number of grooms n is between 1 and 100 inclusive.
The counts a and b are between 0 and 15 inclusive.
The number of grooms is strictly greater than the sum of a and b.

preconditions.expression: isinstance(n, int) and isinstance(a, int) and isinstance(b, int)
preconditions.description: Input values n, a, and b are integers.

postconditions.expression: output == '-1' or (len(seq) == n and all(1 <= x <= 50000 for x in seq) and count_oh(seq) == a and count_wow(seq) == b)
postconditions.description: Output is either -1 (if no solution exists) or a sequence of n integers between 1 and 50000 that produces exactly a 'Oh...' and b 'Wow!' reactions.

postconditions.expression: count_oh(seq) == sum(1 for i in range(1, n) if seq[i] > max(seq[:i]))
postconditions.description: The count of 'Oh...' reactions equals the number of grooms (after the first) whose fortune is strictly greater than the maximum fortune of all previous grooms.

postconditions.expression: count_wow(seq) == sum(1 for i in range(1, n) if seq[i] > sum(seq[:i]))
postconditions.description: The count of 'Wow!' reactions equals the number of grooms (after the first) whose fortune is strictly greater than the sum of all previous grooms' fortunes.

postconditions.expression: all(not (seq[i] > max(seq[:i]) and seq[i] > sum(seq[:i])) for i in range(1, n))
postconditions.description: No groom triggers both 'Oh...' and 'Wow!' simultaneously; if a groom is richer than the sum of previous ones, they are implicitly richer than the max, so the 'Wow!' case excludes the 'Oh...' count.
